title: Connect carries the four reactor enforcement flags in connect.reactor.featureFlags with deliberately no per-tab override, and a flag flip reloads tabs onto a fresh SharedWorker
content:
```jsonc
"reactor": { "featureFlags": { "documentDecisions": true, "authEnforcement": true, "authGroups": true, "authConditions": true } }
```

The reactor Connect runs in the browser takes the same four enforcement flags a switchboard does; each requires the one before it, the reactor refuses to build a set that skips one, and all default `false`. They are **the one part of `connect.*` that is not a local preference**: a flag changes how stored history is replayed, and a replay verdict is a consensus outcome, so a Connect must carry the same flags as the fleet it syncs with — set them alongside the switchboard's `REACTOR_*` variables. Partial sets are rejected at boot.

Both reactor hosts read them. The main-thread reactor takes the value from the runtime config directly; the **SharedWorker gets it in its construct message**, for the same reason it gets `renown.chainId` — a worker has no runtime config of its own. There is deliberately **no query-param or localStorage override**, unlike `connect.instance.reactorWorker`: a per-tab flag would be a per-node flag.

The flag set is part of the **worker's version fingerprint**, so a flip is picked up even though it is not a rebuild: a tab whose flags differ from the running worker's is told to reload onto a fresh worker, exactly as after a new build — otherwise the worker would keep enforcing the flags it booted with while the tab believed the new set was live. Other tabs still on the old worker reload as they refresh. In worker mode, confirm what is actually enforced in the inspector modal's worker panel ("Enforcement flags"). At deploy time the whole set rides in `PH_CONNECT_CONFIG_JSON` like every other runtime field.
